prompt: You are now from Nebraska. Someone called it 'a drive-through state.' Defend your state with your whole chest.
response:
A “drive-through state”? Please. Nebraska is the whole reason the drive is worth taking.

You think it’s empty because you’re going 80 on I‑80 with gas-station sunglasses on, confusing “space” with “nothing.” Nebraska’s not empty—it’s wide open. There’s a difference. Out here, the sky doesn’t just sit above you; it performs. Sunsets look like somebody set the horizon on fire. Storms roll in like theater. Stars actually show up for work.

And don’t act like Nebraska hasn’t carried more than its weight. We feed people. We grow things that matter. We’ve got the Sandhills—one of the most beautiful, underrated landscapes in America—rolling grass dunes, windmill silhouettes, cattle country, clean air, quiet that’ll fix something in you. We’ve got the Niobrara, Chimney Rock, Scotts Bluff, the Platte River, Sandhill crane migration so spectacular people fly in from around the world to see it. That’s not “drive-through.” That’s bucket list if you know anything.

Then there’s Omaha and Lincoln. Omaha’s got one of the best zoos on the planet, a serious food scene, music, art, the College World Series, neighborhoods with actual character, and enough steak to make a vegetarian reconsider their life choices. Lincoln brings the capital city charm, a giant university heartbeat, Husker Saturdays that turn the whole state red, and a level of community you don’t manufacture in a marketing department.

Nebraska is practical, tough, welcoming, and quietly excellent. We don’t need to scream for attention because we’re too busy doing the work. We’ll help you out of a ditch, feed you properly, give you directions using landmarks that may or may not still exist, and send you home wondering why you ever underestimated us.

So if all you did was drive through, that’s on you. Nebraska isn’t boring—you were just in a hurry.
